text: pd.adjust() asks single quantity, pi0: upper bound, set , prior probability sign opposite claimed one. pi0 used every parameter, also upper bound expected proportion parameters family claimed side, null effects included, judgment many null effects family contain can guide choice. Alternatively, p0 largest prior probability claim family correct, pi0 = p0^(1/m) m tests independent priori, pi0 grows number tests. claim made holds every prior lowers prior odds either direction pi0/(1 - pi0), raises threshold pd c (default 0.975) c*.
code: library(multibayes) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(4000, mu = c(1, 0.2, 3), Sigma = diag(3)) colnames(draws) <- c("b1", "b2", "b3") pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi0 = 0.7)   # claim a direction when pd.adj > c (pd > c*) joint(draws)                          # joint probability of the top-k claims

what: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: Converts upper bound, set researcher, prior probability sign opposite claimed one threshold pd must exceed direction claimed. function accepts either vector pre-computed pd values matrix posterior draws, pd values computed internally. direction-agnostic directional tests supported: direction argument controls pd computed per hypothesis. threshold governed \(\pi_0\) (argument pi0), upper bound prior probability parameter lies side null.value opposite claimed one (equals null.value). Equivalently, one may supply \(\Pr(H_0)\) (argument p0), largest prior probability claim family correct, \(\pi_0 = \Pr(H_0)^{1/m}\) recovered parameters independent priori. hypothesis function also reports pd.adj, posterior probability claimed direction (favoured predicted) prior class skeptical ; prior side probability 1 - pd.adj, two sum one. direction claimed pd.adj exceeds \(c\), \(pd > c^*\).

Values 0.5 set 0.5, warning, penalty applied. Supply either pi0 p0, . null.value Numeric scalar vector. null (reference) value posterior evaluated, specified scale posterior. single scalar applies null parameters; vector length ncol(draws) assigns distinct null parameter. Ignored pd supplied directly. Defaults 0. class priors behind threshold defined within-model prior symmetric null value (see Details), holds flat priors priors centred . direction Character vector "greater", "less", "two.sided" (NULL). Specifies testing mode hypothesis: "greater" positive directional test (\(\Pr(\theta > \theta_\text{null})\)), "less" negative directional test (\(\Pr(\theta < \theta_\text{null})\)), "two.sided" direction-agnostic testing (maximum sides). scalar recycled match number parameters; mixed vector allows different modes across hypotheses. title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: object class pd_adjust (data.frame dedicated print.pd_adjust method), one row per hypothesis. Columns: pd (probability direction, compared threshold.adj), pd.adj (posterior probability claimed direction prior class skeptical , compared threshold), pi0, m, direction. order = TRUE rows sorted decreasing pd. draws supplied, output additionally includes median.est (posterior median per parameter) null.value. print method shows \(m\), \(\pi_0\), thresholds \(c\) \(c^*\), columns constant across rows (null.value, direction) header, followed per-test table; columns remain available programmatic access. object also carries, attributes, threshold threshold (\(c\)), adjusted threshold threshold.adj (\(c^*\)), corresponding two-sided per-test Type error rates alpha.nominal (\(2(1-c)\)) alpha.eff (\(2(1-c^*)\)); retrieve , e.g., attr(x, "threshold.adj"). threshold threshold.adj exact function \(c\) \(\pi_0\), reported per-test rate alpha.eff uses identity \(\alpha = 2(1 - c)\), holds null pd approximately uniform \([0.5, 1]\).

title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
text: Following Jeffreys (1938) Westfall et al. (1997), prior odds directional claim family penalized. pi0 penalty number tests; p0, \(\pi_0 = \Pr(H_0)^{1/m}\) penalty grows number tests. direction claim chosen data, penalty applied class priors: within-model prior reweighted two sides null.value, prior probability direction lies \(1-\pi_0\) \(\pi_0\), claim made posterior probability exceeds \(c\) every prior class. parameters independent posteriors, equivalent $$pd > c^*, \qquad c^* = \frac{c\,\pi_0}{(1-c)(1-\pi_0) + c\,\pi_0},$$ function reports \(c^*\) (threshold.adj). smallest posterior probability reached prior gives claimed direction probability \(1 - \pi_0\); prior posterior probability claimed direction $$pd_{adj} = \frac{pd\,(1-\pi_0)}{pd\,(1-\pi_0) + (1-pd)\,\pi_0},$$ reported pd.adj, \(pd_{adj} > c\) \(pd > c^*\). correlated posteriors, bound class can stricter rule. posterior used estimation modified. class defined within-model prior symmetric null.value, priors centred , limit, flat priors. Direction-agnostic tests ("two.sided"): pd \(\max\!\big(\Pr(\theta > \theta_\text{null} \mid y),\, \Pr(\theta < \theta_\text{null} \mid y)\big)\) \([0.5, 1]\), claim made favoured direction \(pd > c^*\). Directional tests ("greater" "less"): pd posterior mass predicted side, \([0, 1]\), predicted direction claimed \(pd > c^*\). Mixed use directional direction-agnostic tests within call supported: element direction handled independently, threshold \(c^*\) applies hypotheses regardless directionality.

title: Prior-odds threshold for the Probability of Direction pd — pd.adjust
code: # From a vector of pd values pd_values <- c(H1 = 0.999, H2 = 0.946, H3 = 0.813, H4 = 0.763, H5 = 0.891, H6 = 0.987) pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, p0 = 0.4) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi0 = 0.8584 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9958 #>   direction = two.sided #>  #>       pd pd.adj #> H1 0.999 0.9940 #> H2 0.946 0.7430 #> H3 0.813 0.4177 #> H4 0.763 0.3469 #> H5 0.891 0.5742 #> H6 0.987 0.9261 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(claimed direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj > 0.975, or equivalently pd > 0.9958.  # Equivalent call specifying pi0 directly pd.adjust(pd = pd_values, pi0 = 0.4^(1/6)) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi0 = 0.8584 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9958 #>   direction = two.sided #>  #>       pd pd.adj #> H1 0.999 0.9940 #> H2 0.946 0.7430 #> H3 0.813 0.4177 #> H4 0.763 0.3469 #> H5 0.891 0.5742 #> H6 0.987 0.9261 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(claimed direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj > 0.975, or equivalently pd > 0.9958.  # Simulate draws Sigma <- matrix(0, nrow = 6, ncol = 6); diag(Sigma) <- 1 mu    <- c(1, -0.1, 0.8, 0, 2, 3) draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n = 4000, mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma) colnames(draws) <- c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6")  # From posterior draws pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi0 = 0.7, null.value = 0) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi0 = 0.7 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9891 #>   null value = 0, direction = two.sided #>  #>    median.est     pd pd.adj #> H1     0.9860 0.8358 0.6856 #> H2    -0.1175 0.5350 0.3302 #> H3     0.7761 0.7822 0.6062 #> H4    -0.0089 0.5030 0.3025 #> H5     1.9500 0.9762 0.9463 #> H6     2.9866 0.9995 0.9988 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(claimed direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj > 0.975, or equivalently pd > 0.9891.  # Order the rows by strength of evidence pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi0 = 0.7, null.value = 0, order = TRUE) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi0 = 0.7 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9891 #>   null value = 0, direction = two.sided #>  #>    median.est     pd pd.adj #> H6     2.9866 0.9995 0.9988 #> H5     1.9500 0.9762 0.9463 #> H1     0.9860 0.8358 0.6856 #> H3     0.7761 0.7822 0.6062 #> H2    -0.1175 0.5350 0.3302 #> H4    -0.0089 0.5030 0.3025 #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(claimed direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it; 1 - pd.adj is the probability of the other side under that prior. #> Claim a direction when pd.adj > 0.975, or equivalently pd > 0.9891.  # Mix of directional and agnostic tests with parameter-specific nulls pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi0 = 0.6, null.value = c(0.2, 0, 0.2, 0, 0.5, 0.5),           direction = c("greater", "two.sided", "greater",           "two.sided", "greater", "greater")) #> Prior-odds threshold for directional claims #>   m = 6, pi0 = 0.6 #>   c = 0.975, c* = 0.9832 #>  #>    median.est null.value     pd pd.adj direction #> H1     0.9860        0.2 0.7820 0.7051   greater #> H2    -0.1175        0.0 0.5350 0.4341 two.sided #> H3     0.7761        0.2 0.7230 0.6350   greater #> H4    -0.0089        0.0 0.5030 0.4029 two.sided #> H5     1.9500        0.5 0.9285 0.8965   greater #> H6     2.9866        0.5 0.9948 0.9921   greater #>  #> pd.adj: Pr(claimed direction | y) under the prior in the class most skeptical #>         of it;
